summary: Three closed European citizenship-by-investment schemes. Montenegro (2019-2022) is the best documented: the founding decision and its amendments are stored from the official gazette, and the Commission's yearly reports give counts by nationality; the government's own 2026 status reports could only be read through press coverage (1,113 applications, 869 approved, EUR 251 million into hotel projects, EUR 43.6 million in fees). Moldova (2018-2020) and Bulgaria (to 2022) rest on Commission documents, laws read in a browser (Bulgaria) and press reports of official figures; key Moldovan legal texts were behind a Cloudflare wall and no Bulgarian official site was downloadable.

programs.name: Posebni program ulaganja od posebnog značaja za privredni i ekonomski interes Crne Gore (Special Investment Programme of Special Importance for the Economic Interest of Montenegro; "economic citizenship")
programs.notes: Created by Government decision of 22 Nov 2018 (Službeni list CG 79/2018); applications from 1 Jan 2019. Applicant pays EUR 100,000 into an escrow account for less developed municipalities and invests at least EUR 450,000 (Podgorica or coast) or EUR 250,000 (north/centre) in a government-listed development project (in practice condo-hotel units), plus fees of EUR 15,000 per applicant and EUR 10,000 per family member. From 31 Dec 2021 an extra EUR 100,000 to the Innovation Fund. Cap of 2,000 decisions. Applications only through licensed intermediary agents (Henley & Partners, Arton, Apex), with due-diligence agents. Originally to end 31 Dec 2021; extended on 30 Dec 2021 to 31 Dec 2022, then expired; pending applications still decided in 2026 (5 left on 1 Sep 2026). 1,113 applications filed nationally, 869 approved, 239 refused; the EC counts 556 main applicants with 1,281 family members. Over 70% of passports to 2022 went to Russian citizens (EC).

programs.name: Programul de dobândire a cetățeniei prin investiție (Citizenship by Investment Programme of the Republic of Moldova)
programs.notes: Legal basis: art. 17(11)-(12) of Citizenship Law no. 1024/2000 as amended (bill registered Dec 2016) and Government Decision no. 786 of 4 Oct 2017 (regulation). Run with Henley & Partners as the government's exclusive private operator. Routes as reported in the press: a non-refundable contribution of at least EUR 100,000 to the Public Investment Fund for Sustainable Development, or an investment of EUR 250,000 in a strategic sector held 60 months. Cap of 5,000 main applicants (CJI). Launched Nov 2018; moratorium on new applications from summer 2019 (Law 107/2019), extended; Parliament abolished the scheme on 18 Jun 2020 with effect from 1 Sep 2020. 38 applications for 98 people; 20 applications (52 people) successful by mid-2021 (EC). The text of HG 786/2017 itself was not read (legis.md blocked).

programs.name: Bulgarian citizenship by investment (Закон за българското гражданство, art. 12a ordinary route and art. 14a fast-track route)
programs.notes: Naturalisation for holders of investor permanent residence. Art. 12a (ordinary): after 5 years of permanent residence, investment of about EUR 500,000 (BGN 1 million). Art. 14a (fast track, added Feb 2013): after 1 year, investment increased to about EUR 1 million (BGN 2 million) or a priority-project route; no language test or real residence needed. Both repealed by the law in State Gazette no. 26 of 1 Apr 2022; pending procedures were ended and SANS was told to review past naturalisations. Ministry of Justice: 50 investor citizenships 2013-Jan 2019 (4 art. 12a, 46 art. 14a). launched=2005 is the year the Commission gives for the scheme's introduction; the fast track dates from 2013.

programs.name: Bulgaria permanent residence for investors (Закон за чужденците в Република България, art. 25(1) items 6-8)
programs.notes: Permanent (not temporary) residence permit for foreigners who invest, e.g. BGN 1 million in concession rights, collective investment schemes or alternative investment funds, BGN 2 million in listed shares or in a certified priority project, or BGN 6 million in an unlisted company (amounts as in the consolidated law on 2 Oct 2026). It was the first step to citizenship under arts. 12a/14a until 2022 and still exists. Ordinary naturalisation after 5 years of permanent residence remains possible under the general rules (language test etc.). Launch year not established; investor items date from 2005/2009 amendments. The Bulgarian Investment Agency certifies the investments: 981 persons certified 2014-Aug 2021 (both stages).
